To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

social media platforms are a new type of medium with a different logic from that which has been dominant in mass media, and that this logic is changing the way in which political communication is conducted.

the network media logic of social media platforms leads to the production of content that is more personal, more interactive, more immediate and more fragmented than the content produced by traditional mass media.

social media platforms, in contrast to mass media, are: a) characterized by an open, decentralized, and participatory production of media content, b) characterized by the distribution of information in the form of social networks, c) characterized by the use of media as a tool for self-presentation and self-expression, and d) characterized by an audience that is active, participatory and interactive.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how online social media have changed the way we communicate, produce content, distribute information and use media.
how online social media change political communication, without resorting to either technological determinism or normalisation.
how social media platforms are changing the rules of the political game, and what the consequences of this are for democracy and the public sphere.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
social media platforms are not just new channels or new tools, but they are new ways of communicating and interacting with others, which in turn change how we think about and practice politics.
social media platforms are changing political communication in a fundamental way, and that these changes are not necessarily positive.
network media logic has a significant influence on the way politics is communicated, but it is not the only factor.
